text:
maria-eng: FYI got the vendor counterproposal for the GPU EDP. they pushed back on firm capacity floors for q3-q4 and added a metering exception clause. attached PDF in email.

sam-ops: ugh, metering exceptions are always a headache. what exactly do they mean by that?

maria-eng: quote from the clause: ```Vendor may apply metering adjustments for 'unrecognized' third-party GPU SKUs and preemptible instances; adjustments may be applied up to 10% of billed compute hours per invoice cycle.``` so they're basically reserving the right to reclassify hours.

jon-contracts: that is a big red flag. reclassification opens us to chargeback risk. we need either explicit SKU mapping in the SOW or a hard cap on adjustments to, like, 2%. also want CLARITY on audit rights.

lucy-cloud-sales: from their side they say it's to avoid billing for trial/legacy SKUs and Marketplace-placed VMs that don't match our reservation. they claim standard practice for some partners.

lia-sre: operationally, our autoscaling sometimes launches preemptible nodes during daytime spikes (cost-saving). will that trigger adjustments?

maria-eng: yes, lia — that's exactly where it bites. They called out "preemptible" explicitly.

jon-contracts: propose this redline: ```Vendor may not retroactively reclassify usage for the purpose of increasing Customer charges. Metering adjustments are limited to corrections for clear vendor metering errors and capped at 2% per invoice. Customer retains audit rights with 30 days to dispute.```

sam-ops: +1. also can we add a technical appendix with SKU list and the exact meter IDs we expect to map to the reservation? otherwise reconciliation will be impossible.

lucy-cloud-sales: i'll ask them for the SKU/meter mapping. one more ask: they want a 12-month ramp for guaranteed capacity instead of immediate floor. they argue capacity planning needs lead time.

maria-eng: our ask was to firm up minimums earlier because q4 product launches rely on it. can we accept a staggered floor with credits for shortfalls instead? e.g., 80% floor in month 1-3, 90% month 4-6, 100% month 7 onward, with daily service credits for unmet guaranteed GPUs.

jon-contracts: credits are ok but need defined SLA math: per-hour shortfall * agreed hourly rate * (1 + 20% penalty). Also need right to terminate if repeated misses (3+ misses in 90 days).

lia-sre: we should also insist on region residency guarantees. last time they routed capacity out of eu-west and latency spiked. need hard region-bound capacity or automatic failover to our Dedicated pool without charge.

lucy-cloud-sales: they'll push back on region carveouts since regional capacity is uneven. but we can ask for prioritized placement and a documented remediation timeline with penalties.

maria-eng: on billing ops: billing-bot, can you run a quick query to estimate how many hours last quarter would have been subject to the 10% reclass risk (preemptible + marketplace)? give a percent of total billable GPU hours.

billing-bot: Running historical analysis... results in ~6.7% of GPU hours last quarter were on preemptible or marketplace SKUs. visibility caveat: around 0.8% were ambiguous due to missing meter IDs.

sam-ops: so if they applied a 10% reclass, we could be fully within their tolerance and still see invoice bumps. not acceptable.

jon-contracts: action items: 1) i'll draft the redline limiting metering adjustments + audit clause. 2) maria, can you assemble a definitive SKU/meter appendix and examples of our autoscaling preemptible usage? 3) lia, compile incidents where region routing caused latency >100ms to our endpoints in the last 6 months.

maria-eng: will do. I'll also prepare a sample reconciliation spreadsheet we can share showing how credits should be computed.

lia-sre: tagging @maria-eng on the incident doc request, i'll export traces and latency graphs.

lucy-cloud-sales: i'll push back on the 10% and the stagger wording, ask for hard SLOs + credit schedule. i can try to secure a 4% cap on reclassifications as a concession.

jon-contracts: also add language for proactive notifications: vendor must notify us within 5 business days of any SKU changes or planned migration that could affect metering.

maria-eng: one more thought — can we get a one-time migration credit for any forced SKU migration (they moved us last refresh)? helps offset engineering churn.

lucy-cloud-sales: noted. i'll table that as a commercial concession ask.

maria-eng: ok team — i'll consolidate notes and drop a draft redline tomorrow. if legal signs off we should aim to close before the end of week to lock Q3 pricing. :crossed_fingers:

sam-ops: thanks — ping if you need infra metrics access.

jon-contracts: thanks everyone. i'll prep the contract language now.

billing-bot: Exported usage breakdown and attached CSV to the contract thread (email).

maria-eng: received. ending thread here unless new updates. :white_check_mark:
